sections.text: Philemon is a personal letter of one chapter. Onesimus, a slave from Philemon’s household, has been with Paul and has become a believer. Paul sends him back with this letter, asking Philemon to receive him no longer as a slave but as a dear brother, and offering to repay anything Onesimus owes.
Paul writes from prison. Philemon was a believer in Colossae in whose house a church met. Slavery was built into the Roman world; a slave who left a household was at the mercy of the owner.

This letter was used in past centuries to defend slavery, a reading that churches now reject. Many readers see it working the other way: Paul places master and slave side by side as brothers, which leaves no room for one to own the other. Whether Paul is asking outright for Onesimus’ freedom is debated; he hints that Philemon will do even more than he asks.
